relations.reason: Forecast predicts future values from historical series; Simulate rolls forward world state under hypothetical interventions and policies.
Planning often uses simulation to evaluate candidate action sequences ('lookahead') before choosing a plan.
Simulation results may inform actions, but should be gated by verification and human oversight in high-stakes systems.
Rollouts should be sanity-checked against constraints, historical actuals, and safety rules to reduce harmful over-trust.

ux_notes.risk: False confidence from plausible-but-wrong rollouts (model mismatch, unmodeled variables, distribution shift).
ux_notes.tip: Label outputs as hypothetical, show assumptions/config used, and compare multiple scenarios rather than presenting a single future as truth.

ai_tasks.elevator_pitch: Discover recurring patterns from aggregate human decisions over time.
ai_tasks.example_usage: Identifying writing style patterns from content a user consistently accepts without editing.
ai_tasks.name: Harvest

relations.reason: Harvested patterns are the input that adaptation applies. Harvest discovers what to learn; adapt updates behavior.
Individual extraction events produce raw data that harvesting aggregates into patterns over time.
Human edits — what they change and what they leave unchanged — are the primary behavioral signal.
AI-discovered patterns are prone to hallucination; verify against source material before applying.
Low-confidence patterns should be staged for human review before affecting system behavior.

Cluster groups items by similarity in a vector space at a single point in time; Harvest discovers patterns from sequential human decisions over time. Cluster is spatial (which items are near each other); Harvest is temporal (what behaviors recur across decisions). Cluster needs embeddings; Harvest needs behavioral logs with provenance.

anti_patterns: Treating AI confidence as human validation
No verification that discovered patterns exist in source material
Patterns without provenance trail back to source decisions
Accepting pattern candidates that cannot cite concrete examples from the behavioral log
ux_notes.risk: Hallucinated patterns that don't exist in source data
ux_notes.tip: Every discovered pattern must link to specific source decisions with provenance — timestamp, actor, and original context — so patterns are grounded in evidence, not AI confabulation

constraints.ux_note: Detect user language, provide language selector, adapt formatting (dates, currency)

constraints.description: How long to cache results and when to invalidate cached data.
constraints.example_values: Cache 5 minutes, Invalidate on user action, Cache forever for static content, No cache for personalized
constraints.name: Caching Policy
constraints.ux_note: Show 'cached' indicator, provide refresh button, warn about stale data

constraints.description: Task runs independently in the background and returns results when complete.
constraints.example_values: Background agent, Async processing, Fire-and-forget, Blocking (wait for result)
constraints.name: Autonomous Execution
constraints.ux_note: Show background task indicator, provide status updates, allow cancellation

constraints.description: Multiple operations execute simultaneously for efficiency.
constraints.example_values: Parallel searches, Concurrent file reads, Batch API calls, Sequential only
constraints.name: Parallel Execution
constraints.ux_note: Show progress for parallel tasks, handle partial failures gracefully

constraints.description: Maximum time allowed before operation is cancelled.
constraints.example_values: 30 seconds, 5 minutes, No timeout, User-configurable
constraints.name: Timeout Limit
constraints.ux_note: Show timeout warning, provide extend option, handle graceful cancellation

constraints.description: Prefer editing existing code over creating new files or adding unnecessary features.
constraints.example_values: Edit over write, Avoid over-engineering, Only change what's needed, YAGNI (You Aren't Gonna Need It)
constraints.name: Minimal Changes
constraints.ux_note: Surface this principle in code review, show edit vs write statistics

constraints.description: Follow existing codebase patterns and style conventions.
constraints.example_values: Match existing patterns, Follow style guide, Preserve indentation, Consistent naming
constraints.name: Code Style Adherence
constraints.ux_note: Run linter/formatter, show style violations, auto-fix when possible

constraints.description: Ensure changes don't break existing functionality or APIs.
constraints.example_values: No breaking changes, Deprecate before removing, Version bumps for breaking changes, Migration guide required
constraints.name: Backward Compatibility
constraints.ux_note: Warn about breaking changes, suggest deprecation path, run compatibility tests

constraints.description: Generated content must credit sources, collaborators, or AI assistance.
constraints.example_values: Co-Authored-By: AI, Source citations, License attribution, Contributors list
constraints.name: Attribution Required
constraints.ux_note: Include attribution footer, add co-author tags, cite sources

constraints.description: Track and document the origin and transformation history of data.
constraints.example_values: Source file tracking, Transformation history, Model version tags, Input/output logging
constraints.name: Data Provenance
constraints.ux_note: Log data lineage, show transformation chain, enable audit trail

constraints.description: Reference and link to source materials when generating content.
constraints.example_values: Academic style (APA/MLA), Markdown links, Footnotes, URL references
constraints.name: Source Citation
constraints.ux_note: Include bibliography, add inline citations, link to sources

constraints.description: System architecture supports swapping model providers/versions without rewriting product logic via adapters, schemas, and test gates.
constraints.example_values: Provider-agnostic message format, Tool schema normalization, Output schema enforcement, Fallback to alternative model, OpenAI/Anthropic/local adapter pattern
constraints.name: Model Portability
constraints.ux_note: Test provider swaps, validate adapter interfaces, log provider metadata, ensure fallback models available

constraints.description: Defines which scenarios, edge cases, and safety checks must be covered by tests before deploying changes to an AI system.
constraints.example_values: Top user intents, Tool failure + timeout paths, Prompt injection tests, PII handling validation, Low-confidence fallbacks, Cost/latency ceilings, Localization checks, Regression test suite
constraints.name: Evaluation Coverage
constraints.ux_note: Show coverage reports, block deployment if gaps exist, document edge cases tested

human_tasks.elevator_pitch: User proves identity or establishes an account/session.
human_tasks.example_usage: Signing in with password, passkey, SSO, or biometrics.
human_tasks.name: Authenticate / Identify

relations.reason: Identity gates access to features and data.
Authenticated sessions enable persistent user state.

human_tasks.elevator_pitch: User explicitly permits or denies data collection/processing and feature access.
human_tasks.example_usage: Opting into microphone access, location tracking, or model-training consent.
human_tasks.name: Grant / Revoke Consent

relations.reason: Consent is enforced via deterministic gating rules.
Consent decisions must be recorded for auditability.

human_tasks.elevator_pitch: User links an external account, data source, or device to the system.
human_tasks.example_usage: Connecting Google Drive, Slack, calendar, or a wearable sensor.
human_tasks.name: Connect Integration

relations.reason: Integrations require authenticated API calls.
Some integrations rely on incoming events.

human_tasks.elevator_pitch: User provides digital assets to the system.
human_tasks.example_usage: Uploading a CSV for analysis.
human_tasks.name: Upload File

relations.reason: Uploaded files are the source for extraction workflows.

human_tasks.elevator_pitch: User enters text data manually.
human_tasks.example_usage: Typing a search query or chat message.
human_tasks.name: Type Input

relations.reason: Text input can be represented (embeddings) for semantic operations.
Text prompts can drive generation.

human_tasks.elevator_pitch: User speaks a verbal command or query to the system.
human_tasks.example_usage: Saying 'turn on the lights' or asking 'what's the weather?'
human_tasks.name: Voice Command

relations.reason: Voice input must be transcribed (via ASR) for most downstream tasks.
Commands are often classified into intents.
Some voice queries trigger generation.

human_tasks.elevator_pitch: User performs physical gestures, hand tracking, or body movements as input.
human_tasks.example_usage: Pinching to zoom in VR or nodding to confirm.
human_tasks.name: Gesture Input

relations.reason: Gesture recognition relies on pose estimation and keypoint detection.
Gestures are classified into meanings (swipe, pinch, etc.).
Gestures can control physical or digital actions.

human_tasks.elevator_pitch: User moves through a physical or virtual 3D environment.
human_tasks.example_usage: Walking around in AR or moving through a VR scene.
human_tasks.name: Navigate Space

relations.reason: Navigation depends on pose estimation and spatial tracking over time.
Movement changes what objects and surfaces can be detected.
Movement patterns can inform preference learning and personalization.

human_tasks.elevator_pitch: User continuously adjusts a control (slider, knob, dial) to steer system behavior.
human_tasks.example_usage: Adjusting volume, thermostat, brush size, or model creativity.
human_tasks.name: Adjust Control

relations.reason: Control adjustments can directly drive actions in systems.
Adjustment patterns can inform preference learning.
Adjusting is continuous; configuring is discrete setup.

human_tasks.elevator_pitch: User defines system parameters, preferences, and operational settings.
human_tasks.example_usage: Setting confidence thresholds, model selection, or output format preferences.
human_tasks.name: Configure System

relations.reason: Configuration constrains how adaptation and generation behave.
Configuration settings (thresholds, categories) drive classification behavior.

human_tasks.elevator_pitch: User chooses from predefined choices without strong commitment.
human_tasks.example_usage: Filtering results by category or selecting an item in a list.
human_tasks.name: Select Option

relations.reason: Ranking often prepares a shortlist for selection.
Selections can drive deterministic branching.

human_tasks.elevator_pitch: User picks one option as the final choice with commitment.
human_tasks.example_usage: Selecting the best AI-generated draft or deciding a design direction.
human_tasks.name: Choose Winner

relations.reason: Users typically compare before choosing.
Choice patterns can inform future recommendations.

human_tasks.elevator_pitch: User initiates a workflow.
human_tasks.example_usage: Clicking 'Run' or starting a multi-step assistant.
human_tasks.name: Start Process

relations.reason: User initiation often begins orchestration.

human_tasks.elevator_pitch: User interrupts a running workflow.
human_tasks.example_usage: Canceling a generation or emergency-stopping a device action.
human_tasks.name: Stop Process

relations.reason: Critical safety mechanism for physical and high-impact actions.
Stops typically cancel orchestration/execution paths.

human_tasks.elevator_pitch: User evaluates multiple items side-by-side to understand differences.
human_tasks.example_usage: Comparing multiple AI-generated designs or recommendations.
human_tasks.name: Compare Options

relations.reason: Ranking often provides an initial ordering.
Comparison informs commitment decisions.

human_tasks.elevator_pitch: User arranges items into groups, hierarchies, or applies semantic tags.
human_tasks.example_usage: Dragging notes into clusters or tagging images.
human_tasks.name: Organize & Label

relations.reason: Clustering provides a rough draft; humans refine the structure.
Human labeling can produce training data for future automation.
Once categories exist, AI can help automate sorting.

human_tasks.elevator_pitch: User adds visual or spatial annotations to content (draw, highlight, comment).
human_tasks.example_usage: Drawing boxes for detection or highlighting text for extraction review.
human_tasks.name: Annotate & Mark Up

relations.reason: Annotations can validate or create ground truth for detection.
Region annotations support segmentation workflows.
Annotations can become training or evaluation datasets.

human_tasks.elevator_pitch: User validates accuracy and acceptability of system output.
human_tasks.example_usage: Moderator checking flagged content or editor reviewing a draft.
human_tasks.name: Review & Approve

relations.reason: Automated verification often precedes human review.
Review decisions can become training signals.

human_tasks.elevator_pitch: User checks data quality, completeness, and correctness against requirements.
human_tasks.example_usage: Verifying extraction fields or confirming record accuracy.
human_tasks.name: Validate Data

relations.reason: Extracted data often requires validation.
Automated checks can precede human validation.
Validation findings can improve future performance.

human_tasks.elevator_pitch: User provides explicit signal of quality, preference, or satisfaction.
human_tasks.example_usage: Thumbs up/down on a response or rating recommendations.
human_tasks.name: Provide Feedback

relations.reason: Feedback drives adaptation and tuning.
Feedback can be converted into reward signals.

human_tasks.elevator_pitch: User reports problematic content, errors, or policy violations.
human_tasks.example_usage: Reporting unsafe output or marking an incorrect classification.
human_tasks.name: Flag Content

relations.reason: Flagged content requires review/escalation.
Flags can become negative training signals.
Automated verification may surface flaggable items.

human_tasks.elevator_pitch: User grants an AI agent bounded authority to act on their behalf—spending caps, scope limits, time windows, or approval thresholds.
human_tasks.example_usage: Authorizing a shopping agent to purchase items under $50 without confirmation, or letting a coding agent merge PRs that pass all checks.
human_tasks.name: Delegate Authority

relations.reason: Boundaries (caps, allowlists, scope) are typically configured before authority is delegated.
Delegation grants the agent permission to execute actions without per-action approval.
Delegated actions should be monitored for drift, overspend, or scope violations.
Revocation is the inverse of delegation—human reclaims authority from the agent.
Consent governs data; delegation governs agency. Both transfer a form of permission, but delegation transfers the right to act.

human_tasks.elevator_pitch: User modifies system-generated or system-provided content.
human_tasks.example_usage: Rewriting an AI email draft or editing generated copy.
human_tasks.name: Edit Content

relations.reason: Generated content is often refined by humans.
Edit patterns can inform future improvements.
Edits may trigger regeneration or iteration.

human_tasks.elevator_pitch: User takes an artifact out of the system into another context.
human_tasks.example_usage: Downloading a report, exporting a dataset, or copying a prompt pack.
human_tasks.name: Export / Download

relations.reason: Exports often require format conversion.
Exports should be logged for auditing and analytics.

layers.description: How the system perceives inputs from people and the environment, and converts them into usable signals and structured artifacts.

red_flags: Assuming input is already clean or structured
Ignoring noise, ambiguity, or missing context
guidance.typical_position: Start of flow (or any time new input enters the system).
guidance.when_to_use: When handling raw inputs (text, files, audio, images, sensors) or converting unstructured content into structured forms.

layers.label: Sensing
layers.name: Inbound

layers.description: Model reasoning, scoring, and deterministic business logic that decides what happens next.

red_flags: Black-box decisions without an explanation path
Unclear decision ownership (AI vs rules vs human)
guidance.typical_position: Middle of flow (can repeat multiple times).
guidance.when_to_use: When the system must interpret signals, compare options, apply rules, verify constraints, or make decisions under uncertainty.

layers.label: Reasoning
layers.name: Internal

layers.description: How the system produces outputs—content, recommendations, summaries, transformations—and communicates them to people or other systems.

red_flags: Ungrounded outputs (no citations, weak linkage to evidence)
Overwhelming detail with no controllable level-of-detail
No affordance for correction, editing, or safe fallback
guidance.typical_position: End of a loop or step (often followed by user response).
guidance.when_to_use: When presenting results, generating or transforming content, creating artifacts, or preparing outputs for downstream systems.

layers.label: Expressing
layers.name: Outbound

layers.description: Closed-loop behavior over time: actions, feedback, adaptation, monitoring, and state updates (simulate → plan → act → observe → update).

red_flags: No rollback/stop mechanism or rate limits (runaway loops)
Unsafe actions without human control points
guidance.when_to_use: When the system acts in an environment, adapts from feedback, runs experiments, maintains state across sessions, or monitors drift/performance.

layers.label: Acting
layers.name: Interactive

system_tasks.elevator_pitch: Retrieves existing data from persistent storage.
system_tasks.example_usage: Fetching user profile by ID on login.
system_tasks.name: Read Record

relations.reason: Database reads provide the corpus for retrieval systems.
Often check if record exists before creating.

system_tasks.elevator_pitch: Short-circuits processing by retrieving previously generated results for similar inputs.
system_tasks.example_usage: Returning a cached SQL query for 'Show me sales' without calling the LLM again.
system_tasks.name: Semantic Cache

relations.reason: Caching relies on embeddings to find 'similar' previous requests.
Cache lookup happens before generation; if hit, generation is skipped.

system_tasks.elevator_pitch: Waits for external service triggers.
system_tasks.example_usage: Listening for Stripe payment success.
system_tasks.name: Webhook Listener

system_tasks.elevator_pitch: Triggers actions based on time schedules.
system_tasks.example_usage: Nightly batch job.
system_tasks.name: Scheduled Timer

system_tasks.elevator_pitch: Deterministic branching logic based on conditions.
system_tasks.example_usage: If confidence score > 0.5, then approve.
system_tasks.name: Logic Gate

relations.reason: Classification outputs feed business logic rules.
Regression predictions trigger threshold-based actions.
Rule-based threshold checks trigger automated retraining when model performance degrades.

system_tasks.elevator_pitch: Transforms data structure without changing meaning.
system_tasks.example_usage: Converting JSON to CSV for spreadsheet export.
system_tasks.name: Format Conversion

system_tasks.elevator_pitch: Executes an action in an external service.
system_tasks.example_usage: Booking a calendar slot via Google Calendar API.
system_tasks.name: API Call

relations.reason: Generated content often drives API actions.

system_tasks.elevator_pitch: Inserts new data into persistent storage.
system_tasks.example_usage: Creating a new user account in the database.
system_tasks.name: Create Record

relations.reason: Extracted structured data is typically persisted as new records.
Generated content often needs to be saved as new records.
Record creation should be logged for audit trails.

system_tasks.elevator_pitch: Modifies existing data in persistent storage.
system_tasks.example_usage: Updating user preferences or profile information.
system_tasks.name: Update Record

relations.reason: Typically read existing record before updating.
Extracted data often updates existing records.
Record updates should be logged for audit trails.

system_tasks.elevator_pitch: Removes data from persistent storage.
system_tasks.example_usage: Deleting user account when requested or removing expired data.
system_tasks.name: Delete Record

relations.reason: Often verify record exists before deleting.
Deletions often require human confirmation for safety.
Deletions must be logged for audit trails and compliance.

system_tasks.elevator_pitch: Sends an alert to a user channel.
system_tasks.example_usage: Push notification on mobile.
system_tasks.name: Send Notification

relations.reason: Monitoring systems trigger notifications.

system_tasks.elevator_pitch: Records system state for audit trails.
system_tasks.example_usage: Logging an error or user action.
system_tasks.name: Log Event

system_tasks.elevator_pitch: Executes version control operations in a Git repository.
system_tasks.example_usage: Committing generated code changes to a feature branch.
system_tasks.name: Git Action

relations.reason: Generated code often needs to be committed to version control.
Both persist data, but Git is for code/text versioning vs. structured records.
Git operations should be logged for audit trails.

system_tasks.elevator_pitch: Executes model training or fine-tuning on ML infrastructure.
system_tasks.example_usage: Fine-tuning GPT-4 on customer support transcripts.
system_tasks.name: Train Model

relations.reason: Training jobs should be followed by evaluation to measure effectiveness.
Trained models must be persisted to storage as new records.
Training data often needs format conversion before training.
RLHF training requires human preference data.

system_tasks.elevator_pitch: Calculates performance metrics for model quality assessment.
system_tasks.example_usage: Running test suite to measure accuracy and F1 score.
system_tasks.name: Evaluate Model

relations.reason: Evaluation typically follows training to validate model quality.
Evaluation metrics trigger deployment decisions via threshold checks.
Evaluation results should be reviewed before production deployment.
Evaluation results are logged for model monitoring and audit trails.
Evaluation metrics feed into threshold logic (if accuracy < 0.9, trigger retraining).

system_tasks.elevator_pitch: Coordinates task execution across multiple agents or services.
system_tasks.example_usage: Managing parallel execution of specialist agents in AutoGPT.
system_tasks.name: Orchestrate Workflow

relations.reason: Planning tasks create the execution strategy that orchestration implements.
Business logic determines orchestration routing decisions.
Orchestration coordination should be logged for debugging and monitoring.
Don't confuse orchestration (internal coordination) with webhooks (external events).

system_tasks.elevator_pitch: Captures behavioral data across all user interactions for adaptation and analysis.
system_tasks.example_usage: Tracking click patterns, dwell times, and user journey paths.
system_tasks.name: Analytics Collection

relations.reason: Analytics provides the raw behavioral data that adaptation requires.
Collected analytics events are processed into reward signals.
Explicit feedback is one type of event captured by analytics.
Analytics events are often also logged for audit/debugging.

system_tasks.elevator_pitch: Manages experimentation infrastructure for controlled testing of variants.
system_tasks.example_usage: Traffic splitting between two recommendation algorithms to measure lift.
system_tasks.name: A/B Test Manager

relations.reason: A/B testing is the infrastructure layer for systematic exploration.
Experiment assignments are tracked via analytics to measure outcomes.
Business logic determines experiment eligibility before assignment.
Experiments must be evaluated for statistical significance.

system_tasks.elevator_pitch: Detects drift, performance degradation, and anomalies in production AI systems.
system_tasks.example_usage: Alerting when classification accuracy drops below threshold.
system_tasks.name: Model Monitor

relations.reason: Drift detection triggers adaptation/retraining workflows.
Critical model health issues alert on-call teams.
Detected drift may trigger model retraining.
Monitoring results are logged for incident analysis.

system_tasks.elevator_pitch: Persists and retrieves adaptive system state across sessions.
system_tasks.example_usage: Loading a user's learned preferences or conversation context.
system_tasks.name: State Manager

relations.reason: Adaptation requires persisting what the system has learned.
Planning requires access to current system and environment state.
Conversational generation needs dialogue history and context.
State Manager is for ephemeral/session data, not permanent records.

system_tasks.elevator_pitch: Converts user behavior into quantitative feedback signals for learning.
system_tasks.example_usage: Computing reward score from click-through rate, dwell time, and conversions.
system_tasks.name: Reward Calculator

relations.reason: Reward signals are the primary training data for adaptive systems.
Exploration strategies require reward signals to learn which actions work.
Analytics captures raw events; reward calculator interprets them.
Explicit feedback is one input to reward calculation.
Accumulated reward signals trigger retraining workflows.

system_tasks.elevator_pitch: Maintains conversational and interactive context across turns.
system_tasks.example_usage: Tracking dialogue state in a multi-turn customer service chat.
system_tasks.name: Session Manager

relations.reason: Generation in conversational AI requires access to dialogue history.
Multi-step planning requires tracking user goals across turns.
Session context is often persisted via state management.
User input creates new turns that session manager appends.
Session events are tracked for analytics and optimization.
